title: Effectivity of the strict finite-operation Roos towers
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E/Q_l, with finite coefficient rings A_(n+1) and the completed constant coefficient sheaf on each scheme. For any scheme morphism f:X→Y and any good integral complex P on Y, the Roos complex of the strict tower Res_n f*(P tensor A_(n+1)) is derived complete, and reduction at every index n is identified with f*(P tensor A_(n+1)) by the adjoint of its actual Roos projection. For any scheme W and good integral complexes P,Q, the same assertion holds for the tower Res_n((P tensor A_(n+1)) tensor (Q tensor A_(n+1))). No constructibility or boundedness is assumed. If a derived object K is equipped with an isomorphism to either Roos complex, transport completeness and precompose the projection by that isomorphism; its adjoint remains the specified canonical reduction isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 099M and 099N(5), naive completion and completed pullback; Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 3.5.4--3.5.7; proof steps 1--3 of lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible.

proof.text: For a good completed-coefficient complex, use the simultaneous K-flat reduction model in coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus. It supplies a normalized derived coefficient sequence, a strict representative C, finite evaluation isomorphisms, and compatibility with all actual coefficientOrdinaryQuotient maps. A generic adjunction argument identifies the restricted ordinary quotient with unrestrictedIntegralTransition degreewise: restriction along a completion projection is full, and integralUnit_step says that both maps carry the larger tensor unit to the smaller tensor unit. The restriction composition comparison is the identity followed by the equality of completed projections.

Restrict C to the completed ring. Use literal component maps for evaluation, quotient transition and restriction comparison. Prove their evaluation square directly from the sectionwise characterization of coefficientSequenceRestriction and coefficientSequenceTransition: scalar restriction and its composition comparison leave the underlying section maps unchanged. This avoids transporting a functor-composition object through the completed scalar action. Naturality of the restriction comparison, compatibility of the finite model isomorphisms and the preceding quotient identification give the successor squares. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles these squares into an isomorphism with the ordinary reduction tower. Compose this tower isomorphism with pullTowerIso or tensorTowerIso, using pull_good or tensor_good for the completed-coefficient operation representative. Scalar restriction by each completion projection is full and faithful because that projection is locally surjective; lift the resulting level isomorphisms to finite-linear complex isomorphisms. Form the ordinary tower using unrestrictedTowerComplex and unrestrictedTowerTransition, whose types directly expose scalar extension followed by restriction. Compare its functor presentation with the operation tower only after verifying unit compatibility.

For any normalized coefficient sequence, coefficientSequence_roosModel presents its limit by a normalized DVR tower with exactly the coefficientSequenceProjection maps. Transport the distinguished triangle along the given vertex isomorphism, leaving its product vertices fixed. Apply normalizedDVRTower_effectivity for completeness and normalizedDVRRoos_finite_reduction for the adjoints of these projections. Naturality of adjunction and cancellation of the finite evaluation isomorphisms give the chosen scalar-extension adjoints; sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy gives IsSfDerivedComplete. Choose a prime different from l only to instantiate the legacy interface; no geometric characteristic assumption is used.

The canonical constant-tower Roos comparison identifies the limit of C with its strict mapping cocone and preserves every actual projection. Naturality of the Roos functor along the strict tower isomorphism identifies this with the operation Roos complex. The restriction-evaluation factorization and naturality of coefficientSequenceProjection compute the resulting finite maps exactly. Transport the normalized-limit result along this isomorphism; adjunction naturality identifies each required morphism with the normalized comparison followed by the finite evaluation isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem integralOperationRoos_effectivity :
    (∀ {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
      (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory)
      (K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E X))
      (e : K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((integralOperationsPullbackComplexFunctor l E f).obj P.obj)),
      IsSfDerivedComplete l E X K ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
        IsIso ((((derivedScalarExtensionRestrictionAdjunction l E X n).choose).homEquiv _ _).symm
          (e.hom ≫ integralOperationRoosProjection l E X
            ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E f).obj P.obj) n ≫
            (scalarReductionRestriction l E X n).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app
              (integralPullbackFiniteComplex l E f P.obj n)))) ∧
    (∀ (W : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u})
      (P Q : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).FullSubcategory)
      (K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E W))
      (e : K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((integralOperationsTensorComplexFunctor l E W).obj (P.obj, Q.obj))),
      IsSfDerivedComplete l E W K ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
        IsIso ((((derivedScalarExtensionRestrictionAdjunction l E W n).choose).homEquiv _ _).symm
          (e.hom ≫ integralOperationRoosProjection l E W
            ((integralOperationsTensorTowerFunctor l E W).obj (P.obj, Q.obj)) n ≫
            (scalarReductionRestriction l E W n).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app
              (integralTensorFiniteComplex l E W P.obj Q.obj n))))
